The Kinks - Tired Of Waiting For You (1965)

Kinks lead singer Ray Davies wrote this song while he was a student at Hornsey School of Art in London. When it came time to write songs for the next Kinks album, Ray was running out of ideas, so decided to record the song he had written in college. The group put down the backing track, but he couldn't remember the words, so he went home and wrote them the next day on the train ride into the studio.

This was a more gentle song until it was decided that it needed the trademark Dave Davies loud guitar riffing. Davies recalled "The recording went well but there was something missing and it was my raunchy guitar sound. Ray and I were worried that putting that heavy-sounding guitar on top of a ponderous song might ruin it. Luckily it enhanced the recording, giving it a more cutting, emotional edge. In my opinion 'Tired Of Waiting' was the perfect pop record." "It was a change of style for us, we got a bit posher! Our material started to get a bit more melodic after that."
